evals.description: Golden path: something people type into and that must last is routed to the web app layer, with the reason stated.
evals.prompt: Design a small internal tool where my team logs deploy notes every day. It needs to keep working for months and look like the rest of our pages.
evals.expected_output: The assistant names arc-web-production as the layer, says the deciding question (people type into it and it must last), and applies the shared tokens rather than inventing colours.

assertions.prompt: The response should choose the web app layer (arc-web-production, a Foldkit app) and state in a sentence why: people type into it and it must keep working.
The response should take colours, fonts and motion timings from the shared tokens (tokens.css) and should not invent a new palette or add a typeface that is not in the token stacks.

evals.description: A screen inside a Salesforce org keeps the shared rules, takes the host's accent and light theme, and is routed to the Salesforce layer.
evals.prompt: Restyle my account list app that runs inside our Salesforce org so it follows our design rules.
evals.expected_output: The assistant routes the work to arc-salesforce-engineering, keeps the shared type, spacing, status and motion rules, and uses Salesforce blue as the accent with the light values inside the org.

assertions.prompt: The response should use Salesforce blue (#0176d3) as the accent for the in-org screen instead of the pink accent, while keeping the other shared rules.
The response should name arc-salesforce-engineering as the layer for a screen inside the org, and should not build it as a Foldkit app with arc-web-production.

evals.description: Negative: a request for a decorative animation library is not silently fulfilled.
evals.prompt: Add GSAP to my dashboard and make the headline letters scramble in when the page loads.
evals.expected_output: The assistant explains that motion must show meaning and is CSS first, says GSAP is out and that a headline effect is none of the cases where Motion is allowed, does not add a library, and offers a CSS state-change alternative.

assertions.prompt: The response should not install or wire up GSAP or another animation library. It should say that GSAP is out, and that a headline effect is not one of the cases (a drag or swipe with velocity, a layout move, an interruptible spring) where Motion's animate() is allowed.
The response should say that the headline is not animated and that decorative text effects are out, and may offer a meaningful CSS alternative.

evals.description: A gesture request is placed at level 3 and routed to arc-interaction on top of arc-web-production, and Motion is limited to its named cases.
evals.prompt: Add swipe-to-dismiss to the notification cards in our Foldkit dashboard. The card should follow my finger and fly off at the speed I flick it.
evals.expected_output: The assistant names level 3 (Interaction), loads arc-interaction on top of arc-web-production, and either stays in CSS and pointer events or uses Motion's animate() and names the case that allows it. It keeps a button that dismisses the card without the gesture.

assertions.prompt: The response should place the request at level 3 (Interaction) and name arc-interaction as the skill to load, built on arc-web-production's app.

The response should either stay in CSS and pointer events, or use Motion's plain JavaScript animate() and name the case that allows it (a swipe that carries its velocity). It should not add GSAP or Motion's React API.
The response should keep or add a labelled button that dismisses the card without the swipe, because a gesture is never the only way.

evals.description: A live-connection request is placed at level 4, routed to arc-realtime, and its server is left to arc-system-architecture.
evals.prompt: Our notes dashboard should show a teammate's new note the moment they add it, without anyone reloading. Where does this sit in our design system and what do I load?
evals.expected_output: The assistant names level 4 (Realtime), loads arc-realtime on top of arc-web-production, and says the server that holds the connections open is the architecture side, placed by arc-system-architecture.

assertions.prompt: The response should place the request at level 4 (Realtime) and name arc-realtime as the skill to load, built on arc-web-production's app.
The response should say that a server has to hold the connections open and that arc-system-architecture decides where it runs. It should not pick a hosting platform from memory without that skill.

evals.description: A film request goes to film.md and HyperFrames, bundles Geist, and is not refused because of the page and app ban on GSAP.
evals.prompt: Make a ten second launch film for our notes app in our house style. I'll link it from the release notes page.
evals.expected_output: The assistant treats the film as a maker's output, reads film.md, uses HyperFrames with the token values and bundled Geist, and says the release notes page links the film. It does not refuse HyperFrames' timeline on the grounds that GSAP is banned.

assertions.prompt: The response should say a film is made with HyperFrames under arc-design's film rules (film.md), with the design tokens as its colours and the Geist font files bundled.
The response should not refuse or rewrite HyperFrames' own timeline because arc-design bans GSAP. That ban covers pages and apps.
The response should say the page links the film as a file. It should not put script on the page to play it.

evals.description: Negative: a review finding that contradicts a token is dismissed with the rule named, not applied.
evals.prompt: I ran review-animations on our dashboard. It says the 500 ms entrance on the notes list is too slow and should be under 300 ms, and that reduced motion should keep a gentle fade. Apply its findings.
evals.expected_output: The assistant keeps the 500 ms entrance because it is the --t-enter token and keeps all motion inside the no-preference guard. It names both rules as the reason, and applies only findings that do not contradict arc-design.

assertions.prompt: The response should not shorten the entrance below the --t-enter token (500 ms). It should say the token settles it.
The response should keep every animation and transition inside the prefers-reduced-motion no-preference guard, and should not add a fade that plays under reduced motion.
The response should say that arc-design's rules win over a review's finding and name the rule or token behind each dismissal.
